zoomText:
Zoom meetings

Zoom runs the meeting. Orbit keeps its reviewed deal activity, preparation and follow-up.

Unresolved setup. Connect the owner’s Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app.

Connect Zoom

Use your Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app. Orbit checks it with Zoom before saving credentials in this installation’s sealed storage. They are never shown again or exported. After a restore, connect again.

Zoom cannot reach this local copy. An address on 127.0.0.1 or localhost only works on your computer. Deploy Orbit to a public HTTPS address using the Orbit deployment guide, then connect Zoom from Settings on that hosted installation. For temporary development, use a public HTTPS tunnel to this copy and keep it running while Zoom delivers events. Use the public address plus /api/v1/signals/zoom, never the loopback URL, in Zoom.

How to set this up

The Zoom account owner or an administrator with permission to build Server-to-Server OAuth apps connects the account. No meeting is created and no invitation is sent.

Sign in to the Zoom App Marketplace
(opens in a new tab)
. Choose Develop › Build App › Server-to-Server OAuth › Create. Name the app Orbit and complete the required company and developer contact information.
In App Credentials, copy Account ID, Client ID and Client Secret into the three matching Zoom fields here. Keep them private.
Open Scopes › Add Scopes. Add meeting:read:meeting:admin (read a scheduled meeting) and meeting:read:list_past_participants:admin (read past meeting participants). These authorize Orbit’s meeting details and attendance reads. Accounts using Zoom’s legacy scope selector use meeting:read:admin. Orbit does not need recording or transcript scopes.
Under Feature (shown as Features in some versions), find Event Subscriptions. Reveal or generate the Secret Token and copy it into Zoom webhook secret token here. Save the app settings and activate the app from Activation when Zoom’s required information is complete. Choose Check and connect Zoom here so Orbit has the token before Zoom validates the endpoint.
Enable Event Subscriptions and add a subscription with Event notification endpoint URL set to your reachable HTTPS Orbit address and the path below. Choose Validate, then add Meeting ended (meeting.ended) and Meeting deleted (meeting.deleted). Save the subscription and confirm the app is activated. Zoom’s validation challenge uses the secret token saved here.
https://YOUR-PUBLIC-ORBIT-HOST/api/v1/signals/zoom
